    Services

    From standing water to a secured roof

    Every job starts the same way: stop the damage from spreading, then dry, clean and restore. Here is the work The Masters of Disasters handles across Cutler Bay and Miami.

    Water & flood damage restoration

    Flood cleanup and emergency water extraction for homes and businesses hit by storms, plumbing failures and leaks — followed by full restoration of affected areas.

    Start a water request →

    Mold remediation

    Contained, careful removal of mold growth after water damage or hidden leaks, with drying and odor control so it doesn’t come back.

    Start a mold request →

    Fire damage restoration

    Cleanup and restoration after fire and smoke — including soot, lingering odor removal, and securing the property with emergency board-up.

    Start a fire request →

    Emergency roof tarp & shrink wrap

    Storm-opened roofs get sealed fast — emergency tarp installation or full roof shrink wrap to keep the next rain out while repairs are planned.

    Start a storm request →

    Structural drying & leak detection

    Industrial drying of walls, floors and framing, plus leak detection to find the source — so moisture doesn’t turn into mold later.

    Ask about drying →

    Flood cleanup & claim assistance

    After the water recedes: debris and flood cleanup, odor removal, and insurance claim assistance to document the damage properly.

    Ask about cleanup →

    Questions

    Before you call

    Are you really available at 3 a.m.?

    Yes — the emergency line is available 24/7. Water and storm damage get worse by the hour, so the service is built around nights, weekends and holidays too.

    What will it cost?

    Every property and every loss is different, so scope and next steps are confirmed by phone after the situation is understood. Call (786) 962-4324 for a direct conversation — no guessing from a web page.

    Can you help with my insurance claim?

    Yes — insurance claim assistance is part of the service, including documenting the damage. The intake form above has a field for your claim status so it’s in the summary from the start.

    What should I do before you arrive?

    Stay safe first: avoid standing water near electricity and don’t re-enter a fire-damaged property. The intake tool above lists first steps for water, mold, fire and storm situations.
